items.title: Parathyroid hormone, pulmonary artery pressure and right ventricular function in patients undergoing/awaiting hemodialysis.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients, with pulmonary hypertension (PH) and right ventricular (RV) dysfunction being especially detrimental. Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT), common in CKD-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD), has been linked to vascular problems, but its specific role in pulmonary vascular disease and RV function in hemodialysis (HD) patients remains unclear.This study examined the relationship between serum intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), pulmonary artery pressure (PAP), and RV function in CKD patients (both on HD and pre-dialysis). The hypothesis was that higher iPTH correlates with increased PAP and worse RV function. A total of 115 CKD patients (69.6% HD, 30.4% pre-dialysis) were enrolled. Clinical data included iPTH, calcium, phosphorus, and albumin. Echocardiography measured pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and fractional area change (FAC). Statistical analyses adjusted for confounders. PH prevalence was 60%. Severe PH patients had significantly higher mean iPTH (P=0.001). In the HD group, elevated iPTH strongly linked to severe PH (p<0.001); each unit iPTH increase raised PH risk by 1.01-fold (P=0.004). However, no direct iPTH-RV function association was found. Elevated iPTH and longer HD duration are significant PH risk factors in CKD, particularly in HD patients. These findings underscore the need for CKD-MBD management and suggest that PTH-lowering therapies may reduce PH risk and improve cardiovascular outcomes. Further research is needed to identify other contributors to RV dysfunction in CKD.

items.title: Atypical echocardiographic phenotype of end-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a case series.
items.abstract: We fully documented the diagnostic process of three hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) cases without typical asymmetric myocardial hypertrophy, including medical histories, imaging, and laboratory tests, ultimately confirming the diagnosis through genetic testing. Case 1 presented with segmental wall motion abnormalities with thrombosis, requiring differentiation from coronary atherosclerotic heart disease; case 2 presented with restrictive hemodynamic changes that could be confused with restrictive cardiomyopathy such as amyloidosis; case 3 occurred in a pediatric setting and showed diffuse and concentric hypertrophy similar to metabolic disorders. Various imaging examinations were employed for differential diagnosis, and whole-exome sequencing identified a pathogenic MYBPC3 mutation in case 1 and pathogenic MYH7 mutations in cases 2 and 3, including a de novo variant in case 3. We provided appropriate treatment and follow-up for each case. Case 1's left ventricular ejection fraction increased to 48%, and cases 2 and 3 have not experienced worsening heart failure or malignant arrhythmic events based on an optimized drug regimen. This case series confirms the diversity of echocardiographic phenotypes in end-stage HCM, underscoring the role of multimodal imaging and genetic testing in diagnosis and differential diagnosis.

items.title: Early changes in CT-derived quantitative flow ratio after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a serial coronary physiological assessment.
items.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for severe aortic valve stenosis, but its effects on coronary physiology remain incompletely understood. CT-derived quantitative flow ratio (CT-QFR) enables non-invasive assessment of coronary physiology. This study aimed to investigate the early changes in CT-QFR following TAVR. This retrospective study included consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography before and within 7 days after TAVR. CT-QFR was calculated for all analyzable coronary vessels. Longitudinal changes in CT-QFR were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with patient identifier as a random effect. A total of 109 patients (324 coronary vessels) were analyzed. Plaque volume, plaque burden, and minimal lumen diameter remained unchanged after TAVR, whereas transvalvular pressure gradients decreased significantly. Overall, CT-QFR increased modestly following TAVR ( β =0.018, P   β =0.104, P   β =0.117, P  < 0.001). TAVR was associated with modest early increases in CT-QFR, particularly in vessels with greater anatomical stenosis or baseline physiological impairment. These findings suggest that coronary physiological assessment in severe aortic stenosis may be influenced by valve intervention and should be interpreted cautiously during the peri-TAVR period.

items.title: Case Report: A severe case of human parechovirus encephalitis in a neonate.
items.abstract: Human parechovirus is a common pathogen causing respiratory and gastroenterological symptoms. Symptoms range from asymptomatic courses to rare encephalitis or sepsis-like symptoms. Studies regarding neurodevelopment after parechovirus encephalitis in infants are conflicting with indications of possible short or long term neurodevelopmental impairments. In this case report we describe an especially severe course of human parechovirus infection. A two-week-old infant presented with fever and developed seizures and apneic episodes after admission. Laboratory tests revealed leukopenia. A lumbar puncture revealed parechovirus via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Recurrent seizures required extensive anticonvulsive therapy. Invasive ventilation for four days was necessary due to apneic episodes. Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed white matter involvement. In neonates with a sepsis-like presentation and largely unremarkable laboratory and cerebrospinal fluid findings, parechovirus encephalitis is an important differential diagnosis. In this case, follow-up examinations showed age-appropriate neurodevelopment. However, owing to the severe clinical presentation and extensive neuroimaging abnormalities, long-term neurodevelopmental monitoring is warranted.

items.title: Ulcerative colitis reporting across medications: FAERS analysis and cross-species transcriptomic triangulation.
items.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is reported with medications from different therapeutic classes. We examined these reporting associations together with recorded clinical context and tested whether experimental cytokine-blockade signatures align with human UC mucosal expression. FAERS reports from 2004Q1-2024Q4 were restricted to health professionals and primary-suspect medications. Ten previously identified candidates were evaluated using unique report-generic counts, reporting odds ratios (RORs), proportional reporting ratios, and a supportive Bayesian information component. Sensitivity analysis excluded complete reports recording UC as an indication. Directional signatures from five antibody-versus-isotype contrasts in a 42-sample mouse colitis study were scored in two external human cohorts (87 UC/21 controls and 74 active UC/11 controls), using 12,109 common one-to-one orthologs. Ten primary score comparisons underwent joint Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Among 7,300,798 eligible FAERS reports, 11,352 included UC. Eight candidates met the specified reporting criteria; seven retained support after UC-indication exclusion. Secukinumab and isotretinoin had 204 and 130 UC reports, with RORs of 4.49 (95% CI 3.90-5.16) and 3.79 (3.19-4.51). Valganciclovir decreased from nine to three reports after exclusion and became imprecise. In human mucosa, experiment-2 IL-17A and IL-17RA blockade signatures scored lower in UC in both cohorts; experiment-1 IL-17RA showed a positive difference in only one cohort. IL-23p19 and IL-12/23p40 blockade signatures scored lower in UC in both cohorts. These patterns persisted across the planned signature-size sensitivity analysis. Event-centered analysis differentiated reporting associations by their indication context. External experimental and patient data did not support a uniform UC-like transcriptional pattern following IL-17 blockade, refining the mechanistic interpretation of the reporting signals. The findings identify priorities for drug-specific clinical investigation without estimating incidence or establishing causality.

items.title: Facial pruritus and stiffness as the initial manifestations of glycine receptor antibody-positive progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus: a case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM) is a rare and severe phenotype within stiff-person spectrum disorders (SPSD), frequently associated with glycine receptor antibodies (GlyR-Ab). Because typical rigidity and stimulus-sensitive spasms may be absent at disease onset, early diagnosis can be challenging. We report a 52-year-old man who presented with facial pruritus, facial stiffness, limited tongue protrusion, dysphagia, and left lower-limb pain. Early manifestations included diplopia, restricted extraocular movements, dysarthria, restricted mouth opening, involuntary jaw closure resembling trismus, and involuntary tongue biting. Nonspecific oropharyngeal and maxillofacial abnormalities on imaging initially raised concern for infectious multiple cranial neuropathy, tetanus, or orofacial infection; however, antimicrobial therapy and symptomatic treatment with diazepam and pregabalin produced no sustained improvement. The subsequent emergence of neck, truncal, and lower-limb stiffness, gait impairment, perioral hypersensitivity, and stimulus-induced facial muscle contractions prompted reconsideration of SPSD. Needle electromyography (EMG) demonstrated continuous synchronous motor unit activity in agonist and antagonist muscles at rest. Serum antibody testing was positive for glycine receptor 1 immunoglobulin G (GlyR1-IgG), with a reported semiquantitative value of 1:100, whereas serum glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 (GAD65) antibody was negative, supporting the diagnosis of GlyR-Ab-positive PERM. The patient showed marked initial improvement following combined immunotherapy and symptomatic treatment. During regular follow-up, the patient's symptoms progressively improved. At the latest follow-up, diplopia, facial sensory abnormalities, restricted mouth opening, and limb rigidity had resolved. Repeat serum testing at a different laboratory showed persistent GlyR1-IgG positivity, with a reported endpoint titer of 1:100; the two numerical results were not directly comparable because different titration protocols were used. The patient was advised to continue oral mycophenolate mofetil 500 mg twice daily as maintenance therapy. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges of GlyR-Ab-positive PERM when facial pruritus and cranial-bulbar symptoms precede generalized stiffness. Recognition of evolving stimulus-induced muscle contractions, together with characteristic EMG findings and antibody testing, can help distinguish this presentation from infectious cranial neuropathy, tetanus, and local orofacial disease.

items.title: TCR clonotyping of paired blood and tonsillar T-follicular cells reveals the mixed origin of CD38 high Tfrs.
items.abstract: Circulating T follicular regulatory (cTfr) cells are measured as blood biomarkers after vaccination, in autoimmune disease (e.g., lupus, rheumatoid arthritis) and cancer immunotherapy, yet whether they originate from natural Tregs (yielding nTfr) or germinal center T follicular helper (GC Tfh) cells (yielding iTfr) remains unknown. This distinction is critical for interpreting cTfr expansion as Treg-derived regulation versus Tfh-derived negative feedback. To characterize tonsillar follicular T cell heterogeneity and resolve the origins of cTfr cells we applied single-cell multiomics and bulk T cell receptor sequencing (TCRβ-seq) analysis of matched human tonsil and blood. Tonsillar nTfr and iTfr cells distribute across shared transcriptional states, with CD38 expression distinguishing iTfr from nTfr in most contexts. However, within a transitional cluster positioned between activated Tfh and Tfr cells, nTfr-like cells also upregulated CD38, indicating that its specificity for iTfr is not absolute. Peripheral blood CD38 - cTfr cells shared clonotypes exclusively with non-follicular Tregs and lacked overlap with GC Tfh, indicating predominantly Treg origin. CD38 high cTfr cells captured a mixed population: some shared clonotypes with tonsillar GC Tfh (iTfr), while others shared clonotypes with non-follicular Tregs (nTfr). These findings establish that accurate discrimination of iTfr versus nTfr within the CD38 high compartment requires TCR clonal reference to matched tissue.

items.title: A novel CAF-related gene signature for prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction in PDAC based on single-cell RNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data.
items.abstract: Increasing evidence shows that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) contribute to tumor progression, create an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and promote resistance to immunotherapy. However, the CAF-related gene signature in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains largely unexplored. In our study, we constructed a nine-gene CAF-related signature and found that it strongly correlated with the prognosis of PDAC patients in different cohorts. Subsequently, we found that the CAF-related gene signature was associated with the genomic alteration landscape, immune infiltration landscape and responsiveness to immunotherapy. GJB2 had the highest coefficient in our CAF-related gene signature, thus we explored the role of GJB2 in the interactions between CAFs and PDAC cells. The results showed that conditioned medium (CM) derived from the GJB2 knockdown group could suppress the malignant phenotype of PANC1 and MIAPaCa2 cells. In summary, this CAF-related gene signature is useful for prognosis prediction and precision therapy of PDAC patients.

items.title: Case Report: persistent diaphragmatic and cardiac involvement despite creatine kinase normalization in anti-mitochondrial M2 antibody-positive inflammatory myopathy with primary biliary cholangitis.
items.abstract: Anti-mitochondrial M2 antibodies (AMA-M2) are a serologic hallmark of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), but in inflammatory myopathy they have also been associated with chronic muscle disease, cardiac involvement, and respiratory muscle weakness. We report a 44-year-old woman who developed progressive proximal lower-limb weakness followed by palpitations, exertional dyspnea, and severe hypercapnic respiratory failure. Serum creatine kinase (CK) was only moderately elevated (peak, 789 U/L). AMA-M2 remained strongly positive with anti-gp210 and anti-sp100 antibodies. Low-level anti-HMGCR IgG was detected on two occasions (0.35 and 0.27 U/mL; positivity cutoff >0.15 U/mL), whereas anti-SRP was negative. Electromyography showed myopathic changes with abundant myotonic discharges, and thigh magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated inflammatory signal abnormalities with muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration. An outside muscle biopsy was recorded as favoring dermatomyositis, but the original report and slides could not be retrieved and repeat biopsy was declined. Without independently reviewable biopsy data, the 2017 EULAR/ACR score was 7.0 (estimated IIM probability, 62.5%), meeting the threshold for probable IIM. Arterial carbon dioxide tension reached 94.6 mmHg. Chest imaging showed no extensive parenchymal disease sufficient to explain the degree of hypoventilation, whereas serial diaphragm ultrasonography demonstrated marked dysfunction. Cardiac evaluation revealed conduction abnormalities, atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP), regional wall-motion abnormality, and reduced global longitudinal strain despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. After glucocorticoids, intravenous immunoglobulin, noninvasive ventilation, and individualized immunotherapy, CK normalized earlier than the cardiac and respiratory abnormalities. At approximately 4 months, CK and hs-cTnI were normal, but FVC remained 51% predicted, TLC 57.5% predicted, bilateral diaphragm thickening fractions 10%-11%, and mild hypercapnia persisted. At approximately 7 months, cardiac abnormalities remained evident. These asynchronous trajectories indicate that CK normalization may underestimate ongoing organ burden and support organ-specific surveillance during follow-up.

items.title: Tumor-antigen-specific polyclonal antibodies suppress tumor growth and metastasis in heterogeneous solid tumors.
items.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity and signaling redundancy limit the efficacy of monospecific antibody therapies in solid malignancies. Here we used our platform of glyco-humanized polyclonal antibodies (GH-pAb), to investigate whether targeting multiple tumor-associated antigens provides integrated anti-tumor activity. GH-pAb (hereinafter XON7) were generated by immunization of double-knockout pigs with human tumor cells. Antigen specificity of XON7 was assessed using a human proteome array and validated by ELISA. Anti-tumor mechanisms were evaluated in vitro on 2D or 3D-cultures. Efficacy was tested in vivo in cell or patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX), in chicken chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model, and in orthotopic/metastatic triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) models. XON7 demonstrated tumor-restricted binding across tissue microarrays without detectable staining in matched normal tissues. Mechanistically, XON7 induced potent cytotoxicity across a wide tumor panel through complement activation, apoptosis, and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis. Proteome profiling identified predominant reactivities against solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), annexin A2 (ANXA2), and cytoskeleton-associated protein 4 (CKAP4), all broadly expressed tumor-associated surface proteins. Immunodepletion experiments revealed that concurrent targeting of these three targets was required to maintain the full anti-proliferative activity of XON7, supporting a multitarget-dependent mechanism. XON7 also induced released of high-mobility group protein box 1 (HMGB1), a hallmark of immunogenic cell death. In vivo , XON7 inhibited tumor growth in CDX and PDX models, and markedly reduced metastatic dissemination in orthotopic and intravenous TNBC models. In a CAM model, XON7 synergized with PD-1 blockade, enhancing tumor control and promoting macrophage polarization toward a M1 phenotype. By simultaneously engaging non-redundant tumor pathways and reshaping the tumor microenvironment, XON7 may overcome key resistance mechanisms of solid tumors.

items.title: Quality, reliability, and user engagement of hepatitis B-related short videos on TikTok, Bilibili, and Xiaohongshu: a cross-platform cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: CHB remains a major public health burden in China. TikTok, Bilibili, and Xiaohongshu have become key channels for health information, yet the quality, reliability, and transparency of such content remain uncertain. On November 12, 2025, the top 100 eligible HBV-related videos from each platform ( N  = 300) were assessed using the Global Quality Scale (GQS), modified DISCERN instrument (mDISCERN), and Journal of the American Medical Association benchmark criteria (JAMA). Two raters independently scored each video; discrepant ratings were resolved by consensus or senior adjudication, and final consensus scores were used for the main analyses. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using linearly weighted Cohen's κ . Group differences were evaluated using the Kruskal-Wallis H test followed, when significant, by Dunn's post hoc test with Holm adjustment. Spearman correlations and multivariable ordinal regression models were used to examine unadjusted and adjusted associations. A total of 300 videos were included, with 100 from each platform. Inter-rater agreement was substantial for GQS ( κ  = 0.774, 95% CI 0.705-0.839), almost perfect for mDISCERN ( κ  = 0.928, 95% CI 0.888-0.962), and moderate for JAMA ( κ  = 0.503, 95% CI 0.410-0.590). mDISCERN and JAMA scores differed significantly across platforms, whereas GQS scores did not. Medical personnel had higher rank distributions than normal users for GQS, mDISCERN, and JAMA after Holm adjustment. In adjusted models, Xiaohongshu was associated with higher GQS scores than Bilibili, normal-user uploaders were associated with lower GQS scores than medical personnel, and longer video duration was associated with higher GQS scores. JAMA showed threshold-specific associations with platform, uploader type, and video duration. The adjusted cumulative mDISCERN model was not formally interpreted because of sparse-data instability; a bias-reduced adjacent-category model was reported as an exploratory sensitivity analysis. Engagement metrics showed weak and inconsistent correlations with quality scores. Among highly visible hepatitis B-related short videos retrieved under prespecified search conditions, video quality varied by assessment instrument, platform, and uploader type. Adjusted associations were instrument- or threshold-specific, and engagement metrics should not be treated as proxies for reliability or transparency.

items.title: A single anion exchange chromatography step enables scalable, high-yield purification of hepatitis B virus capsid virus-like particles.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) causes a significant global health burden. The HBV core (HBc) protein forms the HBV capsid and has a crucial role in the virus replication cycle. When expressed across different platforms, HBc can self-assemble into HBV-capsid-based virus-like particles (VLPs), with a wide range of applications in both fundamental and pharmaceutical research. Due to their ability to display or crosslink foreign antigens on the surface, HBc VLPs are used as vaccine antigens. However, conventional VLP purification methods face challenges in scalability and achieving high yields. Therefore, investigating the generation and purification process of these VLPs is of high interest. HBc VLPs composed of three different forms of HBc protein were expressed in E. coli - D (full-length, 183 aa), ΔD 163 (C-terminal partially truncated, 163 aa), and ΔD 149 (C-terminal fully truncated, 149 aa). Polyethyleneimine precipitation (PEI) was performed for excess nucleic acid reduction, followed by two stages of ammonium sulfate precipitation (AS). For a final purification anion-exchange chromatography (AEX) was performed. Purified HBc VPLs were analyzed for purity and stability by SDS-PAGE, native agarose gel electrophoresis, ELISA, Dynamic light scattering, electron microscopy and host cell protein and DNA and endotoxin assays. The single AEX step method resulted in high purity (>85%) and reduced host-cell residues comparable to those detected in a sample produced under good manufacturing practice (GMP) conditions. The HBc VLP variants yielded 5.2 mg, 25.9 mg, and 27.8 mg purified capsids per liter E. coli culture, respectively. Our data showed that all three VLP forms preserved their correct assembly and exhibited minimal aggregation. We successfully designed an HBc-VLP purification technique for the purification of different HBV core antigen particles. The purification resulted in highly pure and little aggregated VLP. This purification method is therefore well-positioned to accelerate studies of HBc VLPs.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in hepatitis: Advances in diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognostic prediction.
items.abstract: Hepatitis remains a major global health challenge and an important contributor to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. Early diagnosis, effective treatment selection, and accurate prognostic stratification remain critical unmet needs in clinical hepatology. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach to addressing these challenges through the integration and analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous biomedical datasets. This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial intelligence applications in hepatitis research and clinical practice published over the past decade, organized across three clinical domains: diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognosis prediction. In the diagnostic domain, artificial intelligence-based approaches have been applied to medical imaging, digital pathology, and multi-omics data to enhance the detection, classification, and staging of liver disease. In the therapeutic domain, machine learning models have been increasingly deployed to support drug discovery, optimize therapeutic regimens, and predict individual treatment responses. In the prognostic domain, artificial intelligence-driven models have shown promising performance in predicting disease progression, survival outcomes, and clinical complications. Nevertheless, key limitations persist, including data heterogeneity, limited external generalizability, and barriers to clinical translation. Future progress will depend on prospective multicenter evaluation, use of interoperable multimodal data, development of transparent models that account for uncertainty, and evidence that artificial intelligence improves clinical decisions and patient outcomes rather than performance metrics alone.
items.journal: The Journal of international medical research

items.title: Precise immunomodulation by mesenchymal stem cells mitigates hepatitis B virus-specific CD8⁺ T cell-mediated acute liver injury without compromising viral clearance.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF) is associated with a high mortality rate. Although mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy markedly improves liver function and survival in patients with HBV-ACLF, it remains unclear whether the immunomodulatory effects of MSCs suppress antiviral CD8⁺ T cell function and trigger HBV reactivation. Here, we developed a novel in vitro HBV-specific CD8⁺ T cell-mediated acute liver injury organoid model, which was co-cultured with either menstrual blood-derived MSCs (MenSCs) or umbilical cord-derived MSCs (UC-MSCs). We found that both MenSCs and UC-MSCs coordinate liver repair and antiviral immunity through precise immunomodulation, primarily via paracrine signaling. Both MSC types significantly downregulated pro-inflammatory (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-8, and CXCL10) and apoptosis-related genes (FasL and CASP7), while promoting hepatic regeneration through IL-6 and HGF upregulation, without compromising CD8⁺ T cell-mediated HBV clearance. This study provides critical insights into the safety of MSC therapy for HBV-ACLF.

items.title: Extracorporeal photopheresis for the treatment of steroid-refractory immune related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a multi-center phase Ib/II clinical trial.
items.abstract: Severe immune-related adverse events (irAE) in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) require treatment interruption and immunosuppression. Based on prior preclinical data, in this prospective, single arm, non-randomized phase-Ib/II clinical trial we test the activity of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) against steroid-refractory irAEs in 30 patients (EudraCT-No.:2021-002073-26). The primary endpoint is the evaluation of the safety of ECP treatment for patients with ICI-induced irAEs. The study meets its pre-specified primary endpoint of less than 50% of patients developing ECP-related severe adverse events (SAE). No ECP-related SAE is observed and ECP-related AEs are reported in 20% (6/30) of patients. Overall response rate for all irAEs is 96.3% (CI 81.0-99.91). Colitis-, hepatitis- and dermatitis-specific response rates are 100% (13/13), 86.7% (13/15) and 100% (3/3), respectively. Secondary endpoints include the assessment of response rate of irAE and overall survival. ECP therapy is associated with reduced granzyme-A/B/K, T-bet, interferon-γ and TNF in peripheral T cells and pro-inflammatory gene-expression in the intestinal tract. The 12-month overall survival rate is 84.3% (CI 63.4%-93.8%). Response correlates with a decrease in inflammatory gene expression in the intestinal tract. These results suggest that ECP is a safe treatment option for SR-irAEs and warrant further investigation in subsequent randomized clinical trials.

items.title: The metabolic transition of liver cancer: a 34-year analysis of global burden across the 10 most populous countries, 1990-2023.
items.abstract: The global burden of liver cancer continues to rise, yet comprehensive assessments of trends in behavioral and metabolic risk factor-attributable mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) remain limited. We aimed to quantify these trends across the world's 10 most populous countries from 1990 to 2023. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we extracted age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for primary liver cancer attributable to seven risk factors-two composite exposures (behavioral risks and metabolic risks) and five component exposures (alcohol use, tobacco, drug use, high body mass index, and high fasting plasma glucose)-globally and across the 10 most populous nations. All burden estimates are reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Joinpoint regression analysis identified temporal trend changes by sex and country, with annual percentage changes (APCs) and average annual percentage changes (AAPCs) reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Globally, alcohol remained the predominant behavioral risk, although alcohol use-attributable ASMRs changed little across the study period [1.08 [95% UI 0.83-1.46] to 1.13 [0.87-1.46] per 100,000; AAPC 0.06% [95% CI -0.01 to 0.14], p = 0.07]. Concerningly, drug use-related ASMRs rose by 79% [0.40 [0.28-0.59] to 0.73 [0.56-0.92] per 100,000; AAPC 1.78% [1.68-1.87]], while metabolic risk-attributable mortality increased 71% [0.42 [0.24-0.64] to 0.73 [0.40-1.05] per 100,000; AAPC 1.67% [1.60-1.73]] and high body mass index-related DALYs nearly doubled [8.96 [3.90-14.82] to 16.26 [7.50-25.62] per 100,000]. Marked heterogeneity existed across countries: by 2023 Nigeria exhibited male metabolic risk-related DALYs nearly four times the global average [95.17 [34.23-204.38] vs. 25.13 [13.61-38.01] per 100,000]. Among women, behavioral and metabolic risk burdens increased in most countries, with the United States showing 2-3-fold higher rates than global averages. While traditional behavioral risk factors stabilized, metabolic risks and drug use now account for a growing share of liver cancer burden globally, with an apparent acceleration after 2020. These findings are restricted to the 10 most populous countries and therefore do not represent Europe, the Middle East, or most of Africa, and the ecological design precludes individual-level causal inference. Integrated prevention strategies targeting obesity, diabetes, and substance use disorders are nonetheless likely to be important, particularly in rapidly developing nations and among women.

items.title: Hemoglobin-to-red blood cell distribution width ratio is inversely associated with prevalent gastrointestinal cancers in NHANES and serves as an informative feature in machine-learning models.
items.abstract: The hemoglobin-to-red blood cell distribution width ratio (HRR) is an inexpensive index derived from routine blood tests, but its relationship with gastrointestinal (GI) cancers in the general population remains unclear. We pooled NHANES 2001-2018 data (adults ≥ 20 years). GI cancer history was screened using MCQ220 and site-confirmed using site-specific follow-up items for colon, rectal, stomach, esophageal, liver, and pancreatic cancers. HRR was calculated as hemoglobin (g/dL) divided by RDW (%). Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for prevalent GI cancer across HRR (per 0.1-unit increase and tertiles), with restricted cubic splines and subgroup interaction tests. In parallel, eight machine-learning (ML) algorithms were trained and evaluated (70/30 split) to assess predictive performance (AUC, calibration, and decision-curve analysis), with SHAP for interpretability. Among 39,663 participants, 344 had site-confirmed GI cancer. Higher HRR was inversely associated with GI cancers in the fully adjusted model (per 0.1-unit increase: OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.95; P = 0.003). Participants in the highest HRR tertile had lower odds than the lowest tertile (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.93; P = 0.026; P for trend = 0.028). Sex modified the association (P for interaction = 0.002), with an inverse association in men (OR 0.74) but not women. ML models showed similar discrimination (top AUC ≈ 0.82), and SHAP highlighted HRR as an important contributor alongside age. Higher HRR was inversely associated with prevalent, site-confirmed GI cancers in NHANES. In machine-learning analyses, HRR functioned as an informative classification feature.

items.title: Population-specific transcriptomic bioactivity assessment of perfluorooctanoic acid using human liver spheroids and physiologically based toxicokinetic modeling.
items.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) has been widely used in industrial and consumer products and was recently classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer. However, uncertainties remain regarding transcriptomic bioactivity thresholds associated with liver effects and their variability across clinically relevant populations. In this study, previously published transcriptomic data obtained following 24-h and 10-day exposure of primary human liver spheroids (LS) to PFOA were integrated into a physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK), population-specific framework to estimate transcriptomic human equivalent doses (HEDs). In addition, exploratory concordance analysis was performed between PFOA-responsive genes and liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC)-associated transcriptomic profiles. Median transcriptomic HEDs ranged from 283 to 412 µg/kg body weight (bw)/week and were substantially higher than the estimated HEDs corresponding to the 95th percentile serum PFOA concentration in the U.S. population (0.0099 µg/kg bw/week) and the mean PFOA concentrations reported in human liver tissue samples (0.035 µg/kg bw/week). Obesity class III, cirrhosis Child-Pugh classes A and B, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease reduced transcriptomic HEDs by approximately 31-41% compared with the healthy population, although HEDs remained substantially above reference values. Gene-level analysis identified only a limited number of genes within the bioactivity exposure ratio range of 1-100. More than 50% of PFOA-responsive genes exhibited concordant expression patterns with LIHC-associated transcriptomic profiles. Although the biological significance of these overlaps remains uncertain, concordance significantly exceeded that expected by chance from a background gene set and was driven mainly by down-regulated genes. Overall, this study provides a population-informed framework for integrating transcriptomic bioactivity data with PBTK modeling in human-relevant assessment of PFOA-associated liver effects.

items.title: WTAP resists cholestatic liver injury by m 6 A-IGF2BP1-dependent regulation of the nuclear receptor FXR.
lncRNA ZNF667-AS1 suppresses hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma by regulating miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2.
items.abstract: To explore the biological functions, clinical significance, and regulatory mechanism of long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) ZNF667-AS1 in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). One hundred and seven patients with HBV-related HCC, one hundred and five patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and one hundred and five healthy controls were enrolled in this study. Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to detect the expression levels of ZNF667-AS1, miR-210-3p, CPEB2. The association between ZNF667-AS1 expression and clinical characteristics of patients were analyzed, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate its diagnostic value. Bioinformatics prediction and dual-luciferase reporter assays were conducted to verify the targeted associations between ZNF667-AS1 and miR-210-3p, as well as between miR-210-3p and CPEB2. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and Transwell assays were applied to assess the biological functions of HCC cells after cell transfection. The expression levels of ZNF667-AS1 and CPEB2 were significantly downregulated in tissue samples from patients with HBV-related HCC and in HBV-associated HCC cell lines. ROC curve analysis showed the area under the curve (AUC) of ZNF667-AS1 for diagnosing HBV-related HCC from CHB reached 0.841. miR-210-3p was validated as a direct target of ZNF667-AS1, and a significant negative correlation was observed between their expression levels. Overexpression of ZNF667-AS1 inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells, whereas this inhibitory effect was reversed by transfection with miR-210-3p mimic. LncRNA ZNF667-AS1 is downregulated in HBV-related HCC and exerts in vitro tumor‑suppressive effects by targeting miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2 expression, thus providing a potential auxiliary biomarker for HBV-related HCC diagnosis and a novel regulatory axis for understanding disease pathogenesis.
